name: Chalcolepidius lenzi
intro: In August 2021 I set up a female Chalcolepidius lenzi in a ventilated gallon tub. I was keeping a female Chalcolepidius smaragdinus at the same time. Each had her own enclosure, which let me keep the two species separate from the start.

facts.title: Container
facts.text: One US gallon (3.8 L), well ventilated

facts.title: Floor
facts.text: 1.3 in (3.3 cm) of moist coconut fiber with bark flats

sections.title: Setting up the female
sections.text: I gave the female about 1.3 inches (3.3 cm) of moist coconut fiber. I laid flat pieces of bark on top. They gave her a place to rest and something to push against when she landed on her back. If I repeated the trial, I would arrange the bark so I could lift a single piece and examine its underside while leaving the rest in place.

sections.title: Where I would look for eggs
sections.text: My 2021 setup documents how I housed an adult. For a breeding attempt, my closest comparison is Chalcolepidius webbi. In that species Alan found eggs on bark or paper towel and reared the larvae individually. I would inspect those surfaces as well as the coir before replacing anything in a lenzi enclosure. I have no egg count or reared adult to assign to my 2021 female.

sections.title: Comparing the adults
sections.text: When identifying another female, I would examine the antennae in addition to the body color. Casari describes the female antennae of C. lenzi as saw-toothed, with stronger teeth in the male. I keep locality and species labels with the enclosure because colors can vary in this genus.

sources.title: My two adult housing trials, August 2021
